name: How much does bathroom countertop replacement usually cost?

mainEntity.name: How much does bathroom countertop replacement usually cost?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Replacement cost depends mainly on the countertop material, custom cutting, sink style, backsplash, demolition, and whether the vanity needs repair. A broad planning range is roughly $150–$400 for some prefabricated laminate or cultured-marble tops and about $900–$2,500 or more for custom stone with an undermount cutout, before unusual project conditions.

**Context:** Actual pricing can differ substantially for small bathrooms because fabrication, delivery, and installation may create minimum charges. A coordinated bathroom project may also include plumbing, electrical, tile, or cabinet work that is separate from the top itself.

**Key factors:**
- Material and edge profile.
- Drop-in, vessel, or undermount sink cutout.
- Backsplash, side splash, demolition, and disposal.
- Cabinet repairs or wall corrections.

**Practical guidance:** Request an itemized estimate that separates the top, cutouts, sink installation, removal, disposal, labor, and related work. Compare quotes using the same material thickness, sink specification, and finish.

Elite Remodeling & Design can assess whether a countertop-only replacement or a broader bathroom update better fits the existing space.
acceptedAnswer.description: Bathroom countertop replacement may range from roughly $150–$400 for some prefabricated tops to $900–$2,500 or more for custom stone, depending on cutouts, sink style, backsplash, removal, and installation. Ask for an itemized estimate because cabinet repairs or plumbing work can add cost.
